s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent vaginal bleeding with intermittent vaginal mass sensation and abnormal vaginal discharge
salient_findings: Vaginal bleeding with clots every 1-2 weeks
Watery, nonfoul-smelling vaginal discharge between bleeding episodes
Firm, globular 6x4 cm mass within the vaginal canal
key_facts: 15-month history of vaginal bleeding
Intermittent sensation of a mass in the vagina
Bleeding with clots every 1-2 weeks lasting 2-5 days
Watery, nonfoul-smelling vaginal discharge between bleeding episodes
Occasional postcoital bleeding
Denies dyspnea, palpitations, or bleeding from other sites
Three home vaginal deliveries
Minilaparotomy sterilization 11 years prior
Tubal recanalization 5 years ago
Prior evaluations did not alleviate symptoms
Hemoglobin 5.3 g/dL with normal platelet count and PT/INR
Firm, globular 6x4 cm mass within the vaginal canal on bimanual pelvic examination
Active vaginal bleeding noted

shortlist.label: Vaginal leiomyoma
shortlist.why_kept: Firm, globular mass within the vaginal canal and history of vaginal bleeding

shortlist.label: Cervical cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Abnormal vaginal bleeding and presence of a mass in the vagina

shortlist.label: Vaginal cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Vaginal bleeding and mass sensation, although less common than cervical cancer

shortlist.label: Uterine sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid growth and bleeding could be indicative of a malignant uterine tumor

shortlist.label: Aggressive angiomyxoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare tumor that can cause vaginal bleeding and a palpable mass

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of intermittent vaginal bleeding, sensation of a mass, and a firm, globular mass within the vaginal canal are consistent with aggressive angiomyxoma, a rare tumor that can cause vaginal bleeding and a palpable mass.

rejected.label: Vaginal leiomyoma
rejected.why: While leiomyomas can cause vaginal bleeding, they are typically associated with a more defined uterine mass and not a separate mass within the vaginal canal.

rejected.label: Cervical cancer
rejected.why: Cervical cancer would likely have been detected on prior evaluations, including pelvic ultrasonography, and is less likely to present as a large, globular mass within the vaginal canal.

rejected.label: Vaginal cancer
rejected.why: Vaginal cancer is rare and would likely have more pronounced symptoms, such as foul-smelling discharge or pelvic pain, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Uterine sarcoma
rejected.why: Uterine sarcoma would likely have been detected on prior evaluations, including pelvic ultrasonography, and is less likely to present as a separate mass within the vaginal canal.
